summary: Batch workers intermittently 403 during token swap — 'resource' claim stripped by private control plane cookie parser
description: Issue summary: BrightHealth's scheduled batch inference workers intermittently receive 403s when performing the OIDC token swap flow. The access token returned by the upstream IdP is valid, but the downstream RBAC check fails because a required 'resource' claim is missing from the token introspection result after the private control plane processes the request. Impact: Causes ~10-20% of BrightHealth's nightly batch jobs to fail; jobs retry and backfill but customer sees delayed processing and elevated error rates in job metrics. Environment: Private deployment (BrightHealth VPC), prod, eu-west region. Timeline: 2026-03-01 01:14 UTC first report from customer; 2026-03-02 engineering triage confirmed reproducible with customer's traffic pattern; 2026-03-04 canary hotfix deployed and observed reduction in failures in canary pool.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Schedule a BrightHealth batch job that uses service-account exchange flow through the customer's on-prem SSH tunnel into the private control plane.
2) Batch worker calls /oauth2/token to perform token swap with the hosted IdP via the private control plane identity-proxy.
3) Control plane performs token introspection against the IdP and forwards introspection response to RBAC middleware.
4) Occasionally RBAC middleware receives a claim set that lacks the 'resource' field and returns HTTP 403 for the worker request.
observed_behavior: Intermittent 403 from RBAC despite IdP-issued access token being valid (token introspection shows active=true at IdP).
Failures correlate with incoming requests that include the legacy cookie 'session_version=2' from BrightHealth's on-prem proxy chain.
No errors are seen at the IdP side — introspection returns expected claims when called directly.
expected_behavior: Control plane should preserve the full set of claims returned by IdP introspection (including 'resource') and forward them to RBAC middleware.
Batch workers should not receive 403s for tokens that introspection marks as active and containing required claims.
logs: 2026-03-02T02:11:08Z identity-proxy INFO incoming token swap for sa:batch-worker-47 via ssh-tunnel
2026-03-02T02:11:09Z middleware.rbac ERROR authorization denied: missing required claim 'resource'
Note: when repeating introspection against the IdP directly we see the 'resource' claim present.
investigation_notes: Reproduced locally using a traffic replay that includes BrightHealth's session cookie; reproduces ~30% of the time in replay cluster A.
Trace shows claim removal occurs between oauth-introspect handler and rbac middleware when the incoming HTTP Cookie header contains 'session_version=2'.

Hypothesis: legacy cookie parser middleware in private-control-plane performs a header parse path that mutates the request context and unintentionally overwrites 'introspection_claims' with a reduced set when a specific cookie is present.
Confirmed: toggling the cookie-parser feature flag in a canary stops the claim-stripping in replay tests.
Related PR fixes parsing logic and adds unit test for cookie edge cases: https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/4312
Dashboard: authz-failures-prod (eu-west) shows spike aligned with customer nightly window; SLI: error-rate batch-worker authz increased to 12% on 2026-03-01.
Correlation: only customers using on-prem SSH tunnel + legacy session cookie observed; pure cloud customers unaffected.
comments: 2026-03-02 09:12 UTC - Support (Lena Morales): Thanks for the report — triaging now. Can you confirm if the failing requests include a 'Cookie' header? Customer says yes, includes session_version cookie from their ingress.

2026-03-02 12:04 UTC - SRE (Arjun Patel): Attached a trace where we can see introspection response before and after control-plane middleware. Looks like the 'resource' claim is present from IdP but missing after cookie-parser runs.
2026-03-03 15:22 UTC - Eng (Marta Li): Pushed a test patch that disables the legacy cookie-path normalization; unit tests added. Requesting canary deploy to verify with BrightHealth traffic window.
2026-03-04 03:10 UTC - Customer (BrightHealth Ops): We rolled a small batch after the canary was applied and failures dropped to ~1%. Appreciate the fast iteration.
workaround: Workaround: Customer can remove the legacy 'session_version' cookie from requests forwarded into the private control plane (recommended for nightly job window) or temporarily disable the token-introspection caching layer by setting INTROSPECTION_CACHE_TTL=0 in customer's control plane config.
resolution: Mitigation applied: rolled back cookie-parser normalization flag in canary and deployed PR 4312 to canary pool. Permanent fix scheduled: update introspection middleware to merge claims and add robust cookie parsing tests. Planning staged rollout to remaining private clusters after 48h verification in canary.
resolution_notes: Canary shows reduction in failures from ~12% -> ~1% for BrightHealth; monitoring for 48 hours. Follow-up action item: add end-to-end regression test in pipeline and ship hotfix to all eu-west private clusters.
